rms_experiment.hypothesis: The existing vectorized RMS reduction preserves the frozen PyTorch mean order for small BF16 batches too; the 256-thread fallback changes rounding at BF16 ties and swaps one held-out nearest neighbour.
rms_experiment.workload: EmbeddingGemma2 BF16, 12 rows x 512 input/post/PLE RMSNorm on RTX 3090 sm_86
rms_experiment.target_metric: exact RMS outputs and frozen held-out ranking without threshold changes

rms_experiment.transfer: reuse existing FP32 square/mean reduction and direct scaling, no causal attention or LLM kernels

short_rms_experiment.hypothesis: The frozen PyTorch reduction uses 64/128/256/512 lanes per row when fewer than 16 rows are present. Reproduce the launch-dependent sum order before BF16 rounding to remove residual-stream drift.
short_rms_experiment.diagnosis: Frozen exact-input primitive replay finds four RMS ties on text-0, including the first changed residual at layer8 PLE post norm. All linears and eager attention replay exactly.
short_rms_experiment.variable: RMS FP32 summation hierarchy for fewer than 16 rows; no change to rows>=16 or legacy LLM kernels
short_rms_experiment.primitive: 16 CUDA tests PASS; all exact-input text-0 layer primitives bit-exact after change
short_rms_experiment.model: gemma-qualification-v5 PASS: all 48 frozen T00 texts have bit-exact embeddings, PLE, all 24 layers and projection; 54 vectors/all4 dimensions, padding, batch/task/ranking PASS. Two additional long-input hidden diagnostics remain non-exact, vectors PASS.

wide_softmax_experiment.hypothesis: The first 1024x1024 DiT drift comes from warp-only FP32 softmax summation. Matching the frozen eager reduction's 1024-thread hierarchy and wide-row grouping preserves BF16 attention ties and the eight-step trajectory.
wide_softmax_experiment.hardware: RTX 3090 sm_86, CUDA suite without fast math
wide_softmax_experiment.workload: Frozen T00 qwen-heldout-0 seed20261021, 4096 image tokens plus text prefix; first block query tile256, 32 heads, head dimension128
wide_softmax_experiment.diagnosis: QK and PV with identical inputs are bit-exact; softmax differs in 21,067,372 FP32 entries and changes 68 BF16 attention outputs in the inspected tile. First-block preceding norm/projections/RoPE are bit-exact.
wide_softmax_experiment.variable: FP32 softmax reduction for width>2048, no model-specific dispatch or approximation
target_metrics: five synchronized timing samples after warmup
wide_softmax_experiment.correctness: First 1024x1024 seed20261021 pipeline trajectory: all eight latents bit-exact to unmodified full PyTorch MATH. BF16 vision follow-up: all 27 vision blocks and complete single-reference encoder bit-exact. Seventeen CUDA primitive tests pass, including long BF16 attention and masked FP32 widths through14461.

patch_workspace_experiment.variable: Workspace ceiling128MiB for full-patch convolutions only. Other convolutions retain64MiB. Encoder request bound unchanged and sufficient.

channel-l2-experiment.hypothesis: A transpose before L2 normalization changes the frozen eager channel-axis reduction's ordering. A generic channel-major input/spatial-major output L2 operator can preserve that ordering and BF16 ties, avoiding accumulated VAE drift without changing precision.

channel-l2-experiment.diagnosis: With admitted cuDNN workspace, the first three convolution replays and first three complete norm/SiLU modules are bit-exact. The fourth norm has one BF16 tie; plain Torch transpose/normalize also differs, proving layout-dependent accumulation matters. Need verify all norm geometries and final pipeline, not infer success from the one primitive.

target_metrics: bit-exact BF16 primitive on actual and synthetic channel/spatial geometries
